The life cycle GHG emissions at different concentrations of H are provided in Figure 3. 2 Maintaining the same volumetric flow rate as baseline NG delivery, the GHG emissions decreased with increasing H mole fraction in the blend, mainly due to the decrease in the 2 downstream combustion emissions associated with a lower emission factor of H . At H mole 2 2 fractions higher than 0.6, the transmission and distribution emissions showed a decrease with H 2 ratio as well. However, the advantage of blending a gas with lower emission factor was offset by the increase in emissions associated with transmission and distribution when the energy throughput was maintained to be the same as baseline NG delivery. In this case, the life cycle GHG emissions decreased by 6% at an H 2 mole ratio of 0.3, while the blend combustion emissions decreased by 11%. The life cycle GHG emissions considering several H production 2 pathways are shown in Figure 4. For H production via steam methane reforming and carbon 2 capture and storage, the reduction of life cycle GHG emissions was less than 2% due to the higher upstream H production emissions. However, such scenarios incur additional costs associated with capturing CO and 2 synthesizing methane. ANL considered various sources of captured CO , including from ethanol 2 plants, ammonia plants, and iron and steel manufacturing, as well as high-temperature and low- temperature direct air capture.
